messages:
maya.dev: heads-up — I found a flaky repro where package "exports" conditional resolution breaks bundlers differently (rollup/webpack/vite). minimal steps and observed behavior below.

kevin: can you paste the package.json snippet and which node/bundler versions?

maya.dev: package.json snippet:```json
{
  "name": "demo-lib",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
    },
    "./feature": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/feature.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/feature.js"
    }
  },
  "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
}
```
Test matrix: Node 18 / 20, Rollup 3.8, Webpack 5.80, Vite 4.1.0.

Observation:
- Rollup + @rollup/plugin-node-resolve (default config) bundles OK for import paths, but when consumer app uses require() path it resolves to esm file and runtime throws "Unexpected token export".
- Webpack sometimes picks cjs entry, but when using conditional exports for subpath (./feature) it resolves to esm in prod build (Terser timing?) — runtime errors only in production built bundle, dev server fine.
- Vite dev server resolves to esm as expected, but edge runtime (Cloudflare Workers) -> runtime error: "ReferenceError: exports is not defined" when consuming the cjs bundle from a SSR build.

sasha: I can repro on Node 20 + Rollup. Quick workaround: make sure bundler has exportConditions support and node-resolve config sets preferBuiltins=false and exportConditions: ['import','require','node'] — but that depends on plugin version.

oliver: can you share a tiny repro repo link?

maya.dev: posted a gist with exact repo layout and build scripts: https://gist.github.com/fake/repro-demo (link to tarball in thread). Steps:
1) git clone && cd repro-demo
2) yarn && yarn build:lib (tsc -> dist/esm & dist/cjs)
3) cd consumer-rollup && yarn && yarn build
4) node consumer-rollup/dist/index.js  # observe Unexpected token export for require case

kevin: tried it — confirmed with Rollup v3.8 + node-resolve v14 you need node-resolve { exportConditions: ['node', 'default'] } to prefer the require path. If you omit, it prefers import.

maya.dev: also hit typings weirdness: when bundler resolves to esm file but types field points at dist/types/index.d.ts, TS in consumer sometimes can't pick up types for subpath imports (./feature) unless "moduleResolution": "node16" is set.

oliver: edge case: Vite SSR + Cloudflare Workers: bundle target expects ESM but the library's cjs export causes rollup-plugin-commonjs to wrap things and produce a mixed output; worker runtime rejects. Workaround was to publish an explicit "browser" field pointing to esm build for bundlers that prefer browser condition.

sasha: config snippets that helped me: rollup.config.js snippet:```js
import resolve from '@rollup/plugin-node-resolve';
export default {
  plugins: [
    resolve({
      exportConditions: ['node', 'import', 'require', 'default'],
      preferBuiltins: false
    })
  ]
};
```
And package.json exports using explicit subpath for ./package.json read -> helped vite.

kevin: fwiw webpack 5 resolution honors exports if resolve.mainFields includes ['exports','module','main'] — try that in consumer webpack config.

maya.dev: build-bot reported CI failure on the monorepo after I added exports for subpaths: "build-bot: consumer-rollup build failed in CI — unexpected token export in node 18 test matrix.

build-bot: CI details: job 4921 failed on macos-latest, Node 18, rollup build step exited 1. logs: \n[error] Unexpected token 'export' at consumer-rollup/dist/index.js:1:1

maya.dev: long-term fixes we discussed: publish dual packages with explicit "exports" mapping for import/require + add "module" and "browser" fields for bundler compatibility; update README with recommended consumer bundler configs; and add a small repro in devex repo so SDK team can test.

sasha: also add a note for SDK: default TypeScript "moduleResolution": "bundler" in recent TS versions is tricky here — recommend test matrix that includes node16/node18 moduleResolution modes.

kevin: short-term patch I put in a fork: change exports to include an additional conditional "node" target pointing to cjs. pushing PR to maya's repro.

maya.dev: thanks — filing a devex issue to track and will add repro link + minimal steps to the SDK repo. :thumbsup: 

oliver: 👍 can we also add an automated test in CI that runs consumer builds with rollup/webpack/vite so we catch regressions?

maya.dev: yes — plan to add matrix job next sprint.

kevin: note: this is very common with libs that use conditional exports + types + subpath exports. worth documenting in SDK migration guide.

sasha: agreed. I'll draft a short doc with recommended package.json patterns and bundler configs.

maya.dev: awesome — thanks team. if anyone else hits variations drop them here. :facepalm:
